title: Conchas
subtitle: Mexican sweet bread rolls topped with a crisp cookie-dough shell scored in patterns
excerpt: Conchas are Mexican sweet bread rolls with a crisp, crumbly topping made from a separate butter-and-sugar dough. The topping is placed on each roll before baking and scored with a knife into shell or flower patterns. The contrast between the soft enriched roll and the crumbling sugar crust is what makes them.
sourceNotes: Conchas are a staple of Mexican panaderias and are sold from early morning. The word means shell, referring to the most common scored pattern on the topping. The recipe structure (enriched roll plus a separate cookie topping) has been documented consistently across Mexican bakery literature and culinary heritage publications.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked conchas once fully cooled. Thaw at room temperature for 1 hour and warm in a low oven for 5 minutes to refresh the topping.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shaped dough balls can be refrigerated overnight before the topping is added. Add the topping and proof at room temperature for 1 hour before baking.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 180 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 165 degrees Celsius. Bake on the middle shelf.

glossaryTerms.definition: The sweet cookie-dough crust (pasta) that covers each concha before baking. Made from unsalted butter, icing sugar, and plain flour, pressed into a flat disc, placed on the roll, and scored. It softens slightly during baking, creating a contrast between the crumbly crust and the soft roll underneath.

. Make the topping first so it can chill while the roll dough proofs. The topping is placed on each shaped roll during the second proof and scored just before baking.

Beat the butter and icing sugar together until smooth. Mix in the flour and vanilla to form a stiff paste. Divide into 8 equal portions (about 30 g each). Roll each portion between two sheets of baking paper into a disc the same diameter as your roll (about 8 cm). Refrigerate until needed.

Combine flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Add the warm milk and eggs and mix until a rough dough forms. Add the softened butter a little at a time, kneading it in until fully incorporated. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be soft and slightly tacky.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 1 hour until doubled. Divide into 8 equal pieces (about 120 g each) and shape into tight balls. Space them on a lined baking tray with plenty of room.
Flatten each topping disc slightly and lay one over each roll, pressing gently so it adheres. Proof for a further 45 minutes until noticeably puffed.

Score the topping with a sharp knife in a shell, grid, or flower pattern. Do not cut into the roll underneath. Bake at 180 degrees Celsius for 18 to 22 minutes until the rolls are light golden and the topping has set.

Traditional conchas come in white, pink, and chocolate. Divide the topping paste into portions and tint each with a small amount of pink gel food colouring, or replace 1 tablespoon of flour with unsweetened cocoa powder for a chocolate version. Use gel colouring, not liquid, to avoid softening the paste.
